fields.title: Create a Critter using TurtleStitch
fields.abstract: Create your own finger puppet using turtlestitch. Use turtlestitch to create the outline for your finger puppet. It’ll then be stitched by a digital embroidery machine onto two layers of felt, and you can then decorate it, adding eyes, hair, etc. Suitable for children aged 9 +

fields.title: Play robot football: program a CoCube with MicroBlocks
fields.abstract:
Score! Your goal will be to teach a CoCube robot how to "shoot a soccer ball into the net".

You'll first learn the basics: how to program a https://www.cocubefun.com/ using https://microblocks.fun.

Then you'll apply your new programming skills to shoot, and score!
fields.notes: This workshop can allow children to work in pairs, but the number of CoCubes will be limited to about 15, so the registration should also be limited to 15 (while perhaps allowing siblings to co-register?)

fields.title: Luanti mod programming
fields.abstract:
The free open-world game Luanti offers a variety of possibilities to
get creative and play together. Luanti is a framework that allows
everyone to build their own voxel game – a world made out of blocks
which can be placed and removed, items and tools that can be crafted
and many more things to discover.

Get to know Luanti and learn to develop your own modification that adds
a new block to the game. Additionally, you can create a custom crafting
recipe and apply effects to your block like making it glow.

Depending on how much time we have, we can explore further topics like
playing together in the same world or programming chat commands.

fields.title: The Human Circuit - a hands-on introduction to awareness of semi-conductors
fields.abstract:
A mini-workshop for families in which they become part of (or observe) a human circuit in order to learn about conducting, non-conducting, and semi-conducting materials, leading to an explanation of the role of diodes work in electronic circuits. There will also be a highlighting awareness of the finite materials in the circuit (Lithium, Carbon, Silicon) in light of Sustainable Dvelopment Goals.
See https://magsamondposts.wordpress.com/2020/09/14/pieu-pieu-the-conducting-circuit-chicken/
fields.notes: The activity takes approx. 30 minutes, and can be repeated at intervals during the day. We can also offer the option of extending the activity to incorporate a micro:bit as circuit output.

fields.title: p5.js web development and more (talk to a microcontroller?)
fields.abstract:
Want to learn website development using javascript? Learning p5.js can help!

In this workshop we will provide an overview of https://p5js.org and share a couple fun examples. We will show participants how to modify and expand upon the examples.

Bonus learning will occur if we can tie p5.js to the physical world via https://microblocks.fun supported hardware using BLE. Our current thought is to expand an existing p5.js "upload image" example. After selecting and uploading an image to the web page, the next step will be to upload that same image to a microcontroller board with display capabilities. (We will first try to use WebBLE to transfer the uploaded browser image.) Wouldn't it be fun to see the same image on the web and a connected microcontroller device? We hope to demonstrate this idea on a CoCube and/or on an ePaper device.
fields.notes: We have yet to figure out if we can teach kids how to make the bonus microcontroller image project, but we'll try. If we don't succeed by the time of FOSDEM we'll update the workshop description to focus solely on p5.js.
